topic: Condition Wait Predicate: Spurious Wakeup Prevention
explanation: Modern C++ strongly recommends using a lambda (or other callable) as a predicate when calling `std::condition_variable::wait`. This pattern addresses two issues: 1) It prevents the 'lost wakeup' problem by ensuring the condition is checked before waiting starts, and 2) It automatically handles spurious wakeups by re-evaluating the predicate every time the thread is awakened, ensuring the wait loop is correctly implemented without manual coding.
practical_example: In a producer-consumer queue, the consumer thread uses a lambda predicate `[] { return !queue.empty(); }` to wait on the condition variable, guaranteeing that it only proceeds when there is actual data and correctly handling unexpected notifications.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
